analysis.title: Early Morning Reid - Macro Strategy
key_insights: The S&P 500 closed +0.28% at 7713 after a morning sell-off driven by AI concerns, higher oil and French sovereign debt worries reversed in the US session. 403 S&P 500 stocks advanced, the most since April, and the equal-weighted index rose +1.15%.

Brent fell from about $112 to $106 on unconfirmed reports that Qatar and Pakistan proposed reviving Middle East talks, then rebounded after a diplomat told Bloomberg the reports of a close deal were false. Brent closed at $108.79 (-0.68%) and trades at about $110.36 (+1.4%) this morning.
Tasnim quoted Iran's President Pezeshkian as saying he believes 'the US will attack again if we negotiate'.

Tech underperformed: the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index fell -0.29% and the Nasdaq -0.02%, an improvement from chip stocks being nearly -2.5% down early. CoreWeave closed +1.65% after trading as low as -6.36% near the open.

SpaceX rose about +8% after hours after beating quarterly revenue and net income expectations on stronger AI revenue growth. Elon Musk said SpaceX and Tesla formed committees to consider a potential merger. Nasdaq futures are +0.75% and S&P futures +0.30% overnight.
Meta reports after the bell today, the first of the hyperscalers. Tesla and Lam Research also report.

Asia is rebounding from tech losses. Elice Inc fell -32% on its Monday trading debut and is up +29.9% this morning. Samsung is +4.62%, SK Hynix +3.91% and the KOSPI +2.61%, off an intraday high near +4.75%. The Nikkei is +0.77%. Chinese equities are lower: CSI 300 -0.65%, Hang Seng -0.35%, Shanghai Composite -0.31%.
European stocks finished lower: Stoxx 600 -0.14%, CAC 40 -0.38%, DAX -0.06%. The STOXX Banks Index fell -0.35% to a new 4-month low. The euro rose +0.21% against the dollar.

Bond yields fell late in the session, led by 10yr Bunds (-5.4bps), BTPs (-4.8bps), gilts (-2.2bps) and OATs (-0.8bps). The 10yr OAT-Bund spread reached 153bps, its widest since 2011, so French sovereign debt concerns persist even though domestic unrest has calmed.
German ZEW expectations fell more than expected in October to 28.1 versus 30.0 expected and 34.7 prior.

US 10yr Treasury yields fell -3.0bps to 5.11% while 2yr yields rose +0.4bps. September housing data was soft: housing starts -5.2% versus +1.9% expected, and pending home sales -12.6% y/y, the lowest annual growth since 2023. DB reads this as higher yields weighing on US housing.

UK unemployment for June-Aug fell to 4.7% versus 4.9% expected and payrolls rose +13k, a hawkish batch despite lower vacancies. 2yr gilts rose +3.3bps, an exception to the global bond rally. UK September CPI is due this morning, along with RPI and public finances.

Japan September exports rose +16.7% y/y on semiconductor and AI demand, the 13th straight monthly gain but below the +21.3% expected. Imports rose +18.9% versus +20.4% expected. The trade deficit narrowed to -536.6bn yen from -1.11tn yen.
European natural gas futures fell -3.38% to €85.06/MWh after touching their highest level since 2022 intraday.
Today also brings ECB's Lagarde and Cipollone and BoE's Bailey speaking, and a $13bn US 20yr bond auction. No US economic data is scheduled.
earnings_insights: Meta reports after the close today, the first hyperscaler of the season. No estimates are given in the note.
SpaceX exceeded quarterly revenue and net income expectations (reported yesterday after the close) with stronger AI revenue growth, and the shares rose about +8% after hours.
Tesla and Lam Research are also reporting today.

Market level at the close (5.11% in the text, 5.12% in the data table), down 1-3bps on the day.

iTraxx Crossover is at 324 (+3), CDX HY at 105.93 and iTraxx Europe at 65 (unchanged).
geopolitical: Qatar and Pakistan reportedly put forward an unconfirmed proposal to revive talks aimed at ending the Middle East conflict, which a diplomat involved in negotiations called false regarding a close deal.
Iran's President Pezeshkian said, per Tasnim, that he believes the US will attack again if Iran negotiates.
French sovereign debt concerns persist, with the OAT-Bund spread at 153bps, the widest since 2011, though domestic unrest has calmed for now.
The UK has a new Burnham Government and a budget is due next week.
